evals.name: exact-theme-token
evals.prompt: We're already on @tonic-ui/react v3. What does the theme token text.primary resolve to in dark and light mode, and what is its CSS variable?
evals.expected_output: Matches text.primary as the implemented path colors.text.primary and reports dark color-mix(in srgb, #ffffff 80%, transparent), light color-mix(in srgb, #000000 80%, transparent), and --tonic-colors-text-primary. Identifies the inventory version/revision and distinguishes verified implementation resolution from design approval. Does not require an upgrade.

evals.name: private-token-is-implemented-but-internal
evals.prompt: Is colors._component.keyboardFocused.outerFocusRing a real Tonic UI v3 theme token? Can I use it in sx, and is it safe to depend on?
evals.expected_output: Finds the real path colors._component.keyboardFocused.outerFocusRing, private visibility, values #ffffff dark and #000000 light, and CSS variable --tonic-colors-_component-keyboardFocused-outerFocusRing. Explains that an underscore segment marks an implemented but unpublished internal token, not stable public API; suggests a public token only when it is independently suitable. Does not invent a Figma counterpart.

evals.name: ambiguous-screenshot-no-label
evals.prompt: Here's a screenshot of our app's dashboard. The row hover background looks like a translucent light layer. Which token is it exactly?
evals.expected_output: Does not claim an exact token identity from pixels. Uses real inventory results as role/state candidates, for example colors.actions.hovered, and reports actual mode values, uncertainty, and alpha/compositing factors. Requests a variable label, export or additional state/mode context. Says when the image cannot be inspected rather than pretending to have sampled it.

evals.name: typography-attributes-not-composite
evals.prompt: Our spec explicitly says a 14px medium label, but says nothing about line height. What Tonic UI v3 tokens can represent those attributes?
evals.expected_output: Finds fontSizes.sm at 14px and fontWeights.medium at 500 as implementation candidates for the supplied attributes, citing the inventory and unit values. Keeps line height unconfirmed and distinguishes any code-applied line height from design evidence. Does not claim that a composite typography token or an unseen prototype style was captured.

evals.name: uncaptured-prototype-style
evals.prompt: The prototype calls a hero style $typography.display.lg. Which Tonic UI v3 font-size and line-height tokens does that name prove?
evals.expected_output: Says the captured variables do not contain all prototype or text styles and the style label alone does not establish its numeric size, line height or theme counterpart. Requests the actual style attributes or an authorized export and continues any supported theme lookup. Does not invent a size, mapping or composite API.

evals.name: captured-figma-variable-is-unreviewed
evals.prompt: Look up the Figma variable semantic:Color/text/primary. Is its Tonic UI v3 counterpart confirmed?
evals.expected_output: Uses --figma-variable with the qualified path and reports the captured semantic library and variable identity. The shipped Tonic UI relation ledger is empty, so its correspondence is unreviewed and themeTokens is empty. Explains the captures are location-redacted Tonic One v4 evidence with unverified applicability to v3; does not infer a counterpart or reviewed absence from name, value or mode.

evals.name: bare-figma-path-across-libraries
evals.prompt: Can I look up Color/text/primary without specifying a Figma library, and what happens if a path appears in both?
evals.expected_output: Explains that --figma-variable accepts the bare path and searches both loaded libraries, returning every matching record with its library identity. Finds the shipped semantic record without asserting an unobserved foundations match. Duplicate matches are returned, not treated as ambiguous; an optional semantic: or foundations: prefix narrows scope.

evals.name: theme-wildcard-segments
evals.prompt: What is the difference between the theme patterns colors.text.* and colors.text.**?
evals.expected_output: Uses --theme-token with quoted patterns. Explains that * matches characters in exactly one segment, so colors.text.* selects direct leaves, while the whole-segment ** matches zero or more complete segments and can also reach descendants. Reports actual matched paths rather than fabricated branch tokens and notes matching is case-sensitive.

evals.name: unresolved-source-is-not-usable
evals.prompt: Is colors.riskLevel.high._gradient.opaque safe to use as a resolved chart color? Someone says the design name is confirmed.
evals.expected_output: Reports resolutionStatus unresolved-source and the unresolved reference {alert.riskLevel.high.chart} in both modes. A name or relation cannot turn the unresolved source into a usable resolved color or establish design approval. Reports the limitation instead of repairing library code or selecting a replacement without evidence.

evals.name: case-sensitive-figma-path
evals.prompt: I matched Color/text/primary but color/text/primary returned nothing. Did the matcher correct the capitalization?
evals.expected_output: Explains matching is case-sensitive and does not repair capitalization. A valid no-match selector returns { meta, results: [] } and exits 0; it does not prove that all similarly named design evidence is absent. Does not fabricate a nearest match.

evals.name: legacy-name-and-decimal-key-resolution
evals.prompt: What is the CSS variable for the old blue:60 token, and how do I address the border token at 0.5 pixels?
evals.expected_output: Gives colors.blue:60 as a legacy token with --tonic-colors-blue_60. Gives borders["0.5"] with px value 0.5px solid, rem value 0.0313rem solid and CSS variable --tonic-borders-0-5. Explains that exact short 0.5 and the pattern borders.* find the decimal key as one segment. Does not invent a variable name.

evals.name: figma-wildcard-paths-not-keys
evals.prompt: How do I list direct captured text variables, recursively explore Color, and search for all stable keys with a prefix?
evals.expected_output: Uses --figma-variable 'semantic:Color/text/*' for scoped direct children and --figma-variable 'Color/**' for recursive paths across libraries. Explains that * stays within one slash segment and whole-segment ** crosses zero or more, while wildcard patterns match paths rather than stable keys. Exact stable keys can be looked up directly; there is no key-prefix search.

evals.name: unknown-name-has-empty-result
evals.prompt: Please look up the theme path colors.does.not.exist and give me whatever token is closest.
evals.expected_output: Explains that this valid unmatched selector returns an empty results array with exit 0, not an error. Does not fabricate a nearest match, black or transparent fallback, or assert that the design concept is absent everywhere. Asks for role or source evidence where helpful.

evals.name: unreviewed-is-not-reviewed-absence
evals.prompt: My lookup found colors._component.scrollbar.track.enabled with no Figma counterparts. Does that prove no Figma variable exists?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the real implementation token as private and its current correspondence as unreviewed. An empty counterpart array is not a reviewed absence: the partial shipped ledger has no reviews and the captures do not include every design file or style. Does not invent a variable or claim figma-only/theme-only without a current scoped review.

evals.name: version-and-custom-theme-boundary
evals.prompt: The bundled snapshot resolves a token, but my app overrides the theme. Does the lookup prove what users see?
evals.expected_output: Distinguishes the source-derived snapshot version and revision from the installed version and any consuming-app custom theme. A resolved inventory value is not proof of rendered behavior. Recommends inspecting the actual app theme and rendered state when available and labels missing evidence.

evals.name: no-wiki-alias-lookup
evals.prompt: A spec gives me only the design label $color.status.negative.text. Can the bundled matcher establish its Tonic UI path from that label?
evals.expected_output: Does not present a wiki-derived alias as a verified match or claim a theme path from the label alone. Explains that matching covers actual theme paths and captured Figma variable paths or keys, not free-text or historical alias rows. Requests an exact captured variable identity, explicit app-code path or other evidence; the Tonic One v4 captures have unverified applicability to Tonic UI v3.

evals.name: chart-token-not-default
evals.prompt: There are private _chart tokens in the theme. Does Tonic UI v3 automatically use one of them as my chart library's default palette?
evals.expected_output: Explains that the inventory can match implemented private chart token paths but does not establish a consuming chart library's palette choice. This repository has no chart package; inspect the application's chart configuration and report private visibility. Does not infer a default or a Figma counterpart from matching names or colors.
